newsitem.title: FRANCE: OLYMPICS-SPORTS MINISTER DRUY SCEPTICAL OF LILLE'S 2004 CHANCES.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-SPORTS MINISTER DRUY SCEPTICAL OF LILLE'S 2004 CHANCES.

text.p: France's Sports Minister Guy Drut expressed doubts on Friday that Lille would be included in the short list of candidates to host the 2004 Olympics.

"I hope the carrots haven't been cooked and we'll do all we can so they're not entirely," Drut said the day after the IOC issued an evaluation report on the 11 candidates in which the northern French city was found wanting.
The IOC said the location of some sports venues, accommodation and transport would pose problems, although it found Lille's bid financially sound with 86 percent local support.
"From the start, I drew attention to the difficulty of the task and warned that Lille would not be a favourite. They have done an extraordinary job," he said on French television.
"We must conclude that we have not quite done enough. We have a fortnight but there are big difficulties."
The IOC will name a short list with four or five candidates on March 7 and Rome, Athens, Buenos Aires and Cape Town are the favourites. The host city will be chosen on September 5.

"Manifestly, there are weaknesses, especially in terms of facilities in relation to the others. It's evident that when you take Rome, Athens or Buenos Aires, the sporting and tourist infrastructures are better and already in place," Drut said.
